content.alt: My first 2 metal detecting finds: a rusted nail on the left and 22 caliber bullet casing on the right.
content.caption: My first 2 metal detecting finds: a rusted nail on the left and 22 caliber bullet casing on the right.

content.text: I got all of my metal detecting gear in today. I went on a short hike into a nearby valley to start looking for things and I was pleasantly surprised how quickly I found things. Within my first 10 minutes of looking I found an iron nail about 5 inches below the ground level. Less than 10 minutes later I found a 22 caliber bullet under about 6 inches of gravel. I had watched a few videos on how to identify different metals from the sounds they made on the detector but it was still kind of surprising that I could tell the first item was iron and the 2nd item wasnt. The stamp on the rear of the bullet seemed to be a "Peters Cartridge Division'" stamp which would indicate the round was manufactured between the 50s and 60s. Assuming the round was fired around the same time, that would mean the round was fired in the suepr early days of Los Alamos just a few years after the war ended. Just the thought that it could have sat there for more than half a century just waiting for me to pick it up is so interesting to me. Unfortunately it started to snow so I only got to be out there for about 20 minutes total, but hopefully the weather clears up and I can get back out there soon.
